transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-10-19
Time: 15:00 PST
Duration: 45 min
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Marcus Chen (ApolloTech CTO), Alyssa Park (DevOps Manager), Ravi Desai (Head of ML)

Auto-generated Summary: scoping Redwood Dedicated for reserved GPUs, want isolation + burst to hosted, run benchmarks, security docs requested

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm Jordan with Redwood Inference, i'm the account lead for ApolloTech, with Priya our solutions engineer. how's everyone doing?
[00:08] Marcus: good, thanks. busy but excited to talk through capacity.
[00:12] Alyssa: thanks, Jordan. we've got a pretty tight timeline for Q1 rollouts so hoping to understand sizing and isolation.
[00:20] Priya: great, quick agenda: we'll ask about current traffic and models, go over Dedicated capacity options (reserved pools, burst), talk security and networking, then propose next steps.
[00:29] Ravi: sounds good - we'll also want to dive into latency for our assistant and cost tradeoffs.

[02:00] Marcus: quick context - we're an enterprise SaaS in logistics, started using open LLMs for summaries and routing recommendations. currently running models on EKS with GPU nodes but cost is spiking and ops burden is high. looking for reserved GPUs with isolation and predictable throughput.
[02:22] Jordan: makes sense. are you on a single cloud provider, or multi-cloud?
[02:26] Alyssa: primarily AWS in us-west-2, some batch jobs on gcp for ML training. production inference is in our VPC today.
[02:34] Priya: good, so Dedicated can be deployed in a private VPC and we also support a private control plane for full isolation, or we can do dedicated with VPC peering. do you have compliance requirements?
[02:46] Marcus: SOC2 type 2 in progress, and customers require customer data to never leave the VPC. we also must use our KMS for key management.
[02:54] Jordan: we support KMS integrations and HSM options for Private deployments; for Dedicated we can integrate with customer KMS via a customer-controlled gateway - we'll share the architecture doc.

[04:10] Ravi: on the technical side, our main inference workload is a 13B open model (quantized) with a lot of short requests and occasional long context windows. typical qps is 120 steady, spikes to ~800 during morning batch processing. latency SLO target is p95 < 300ms for short prompts.
[04:36] Priya: okay that's helpful. Dedicated reserved pools can be sized for predictable throughput; for spikes we typically offer a burst strategy - short bursts served from a shared hosted pool or extra reserved burst nodes if you commit. question: are you okay with burst going to a Redwood-hosted pool or does everything need to stay private?
[04:58] Alyssa: it needs to stay in our VPC for now. the data residency rule is strict.
[05:04] Jordan: understood; we can do Dedicated with a private control plane and configure reserved burst capacity inside the customer's VPC, but that typically requires pre-provisioning and a slightly higher commit. another option is a hybrid where non-sensitive requests can be routed to hosted during spikes - but sounds like that's not acceptable.

[06:20] Marcus: what's the typical autoscaling behavior? we want to avoid cold-starts and make sure KV cache warm-ups don't blow latency on first requests.
[06:28] Priya: our runtime keeps an active pool of warm workers and supports KV cache pre-warm and prefix caching for common prompts. autoscaling is configurable: you can set min reserved GPUs per model and a policy for scale-up based on queue depth. for cold-starts you can do a rolling pre-warm during known windows.
[06:48] Ravi: can we do model pinning and canary rollouts? we need to roll out quantized variants gradually.
[06:55] Priya: yes, model pinning and rollout features exist - you can canary a new quantized build to a % of traffic and fallback to a previous variant automatically if latency or quality regressions appear. we'll show that in the deep-dive.

[08:10] Alyssa: on networking: we run strict egress rules, how does Redwood handle audit logs and outgoing connections?
[08:18] Jordan: we can push audit logs into your SIEM via a syslog endpoint; outbound communications from the Dedicated control plane are limited and documented. we'll share the network diagram and a list of required endpoints.

[09:30] Marcus: curious about throughput per GPU for our 13B quantized model - can you ballpark tokens/sec on an A10G or H100?
[09:38] Priya: ballpark on A10Gs you might see X tokens/sec for a 13B quantized model - (approx) 30-60 t/s depending on sequence length and batching. on H100 you can be 3-4x better, but it depends on kernel selection and your request profile. also batching helps a lot but affects latency.
[09:58] Ravi: what's Redwood's approach to batching vs latency - we need low p95.
[10:04] Priya: we have continuous batching and workload-aware batching; you can configure latency SLOs and the runtime will try to maintain p95 under target by limiting batch windows. there is always a tradeoff: tighter latency SLOs push up cost because you lose batching efficiency.

[12:00] Marcus: pricing - if we commit to say 8x A10G reserved, plus some reserved burst nodes, what's the expected monthly burn relative to hosted?
[12:10] Jordan: pricing depends on region and commit term; as a rough example reserved A10G capacity can be 30-40% cheaper per-token vs hosted at scale, but you'll pay for idle capacity. we'll send a dedicated pricing sheet and a capacity sizing template so you can plug your numbers.

[13:15] Alyssa: procurement-wise, we'll need SOC2, encryption, contract term options, and a statement about audit logging and data deletion.
[13:25] Jordan: yes we'll include SOC2 report, our security whitepaper, and standard contract language around data deletion and retention.

[14:40] Priya: operationally, how often do you expect model updates? do you want Redwood to manage model rollout or will you push images?
[14:48] Marcus: likely patch versions every 2-4 weeks, major model swaps quarterly. we prefer to push builds but want Redwood to handle rollout mechanics.

[16:10] Ravi: about bursting - if we keep everything in our VPC and need burst capacity, what are the latency impacts and how quickly can you scale up additional reserved nodes?
[16:22] Priya: if reserved extra nodes are pre-provisioned but idle, scale-up is near-instant for the runtime; if we need to provision new GPU instances in the VPC that can be minutes depending on cloud provider quotas. for truly dynamic spike handling we recommend a small pre-provisioned buffer plus automated scale-up.

[18:00] Marcus: resource isolation - can we guarantee tenant level isolation and that no other customers share our GPUs?
[18:08] Jordan: Dedicated means exclusive GPU allocation to your account; we can also do private control plane and network isolation so compute and model data don't cross tenants.

[19:30] Alyssa: what about maintenance windows and patching? we can't have unexpected reboots during business hours.
[19:36] Priya: we offer scheduled maintenance windows and can coordinate patches during your off-hours; emergency patches are communicated and can be delayed if they impact SLAs but security-critical patches may require faster action.

[21:00] Ravi: any constraints on model size or custom kernels? we have an optimized kernel from internal team for attention patterns.
[21:08] Priya: we support custom kernel uploads and custom runtime flags via our Dedicated offering but there is an onboarding review. custom kernels may require extra validation and could affect supported autoscaling features.

[23:15] Marcus: timeline - we'd like to run a POC in November, pilot in December, and prod by late Q1. is that feasible?
[23:25] Jordan: yes that's feasible if procurement moves fast. typical POC is 2-4 weeks: capacity sizing, a benchmark run, and a small reserved pool. we'll need your traffic profile and a list of models.

[25:00] Priya: for the benchmark, we'll need sample prompts, p95 latency targets, and test harness access. we'll run tests on a mirrored VPC or white-labeled test subnet.
[25:12] Ravi: we'd prefer mirrored VPC. also can we surface token-level cost analytics?
[25:18] Jordan: yes Redwood Console provides token-level cost and latency breakdowns per route/model.

[27:40] Priya: quick demo ask - for the deep dive we'd like to run a short benchmark with your sample traffic, we can show p95 and throughput numbers across A10G vs H100 and a quantized variant.
[27:52] Ravi: that would be perfect. also want to test patching and rolling updates during the POC.

[39:00] Jordan: recap and next steps: i'll send pricing + capacity template and SOC2/security docs; Priya will draft the benchmark runbook and sample configs; Marcus/Alyssa will share traffic profile and a list of models. we'll schedule the technical deep-dive next week to nail down benchmark windows.
[39:20] Marcus: sounds good. tentative date for deep-dive 2026-10-26?
[39:26] Jordan: works for us, i'll send calendar invite.

[40:00] Alyssa: thanks all. one last Q: any specific procurement docs needed early?
[40:06] Jordan: we'll include standard SOW and contract templates; if you have a preferred redlines list send them.

[41:50] Ravi: ok thanks - excited to see numbers.
[41:55] Jordan: great, talk soon.

End of transcript
